column6: Lamane Jegan Joof founded the village around the 11th century; the Raan festival is held here each April.
The Serer king of Sine, Kumba Ndoffene Famak Joof, defeated and killed Maba Diakhou Bâ here on 18 July 1867.
The Saltigue foretell the future before the community at the Xooy ceremony, usually in the first week of June.

column3: The Serer religion, A ƭat Roog, is the original religion of the Serer people of Senegambia; Lamane Jegan Joof founds the village of Tukar around the 11th century.
In 19th-century wars with Islamic marabouts, Serers at Naodorou, Kaymor and Ngaye kill themselves rather than be conquered, and Maba Diakhou Bâ is killed at the Battle of Fandane-Thiouthioune (1867).
Most Serers convert to Islam and Roman Catholicism after colonisation, though many in Sine keep the Serer religion, and some mix it with the newer faiths.
The last funeral of a king of Sine, Maad a Sinig Mahecor Joof, is held with the old rites on 8 March 1969.
The Xooy ceremony at Fatick and the Raan festival at Tukar continue to bring followers together.
